history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row (seq 2397) is a duplicate of seq 1079 (id mansa-devi-temple-meerut) - same name ('Mansa Devi Temple') and town ('Meerut'), same referent. Merge with or remove from the master CSV. IDENTITY NOTE: several Mansa Devi temples exist in Meerut; this entry documents the principal/oldest one at Kaliyagarhi, Jagriti Vihar (Sector-6). The site is believed to be very old - once a thousand-year-old forest - with some attributing its establishment to Mandodari; worship here is said to fulfill devotees' wishes. It was long only a small shrine (kept by priest Ramgiri, where locals picnicked and farmers sold produce, worshipped mainly during Navratri) and was reconstructed into the present temple in 1990. Known for its exquisite architecture and a lifelike idol of Goddess Mansa; a Sunday fair doubles the crowd. Distinct from the newer Mansa Devi Dham Mandir near City Station (founded by Mahant Shri Anil Tripathi) and the rural Mansha Devi Mandir at Khejuri Alyarpur - verify which shrine the CSV intends.

name: Mansa Devi Temple
town_description: Meerut, in western Uttar Pradesh about 70 km northeast of Delhi, is one of the NCR's largest cities - known as the 'Sports City of India' for its sports-goods industry - and is historically famous as the city where the 1857 uprising began.

travel.airport: Meerut Airport has limited services; the nearest major airport is Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~70-90 km)
travel.railway: Meerut City Junction is the nearest major station (~2-3 km from most city temples); the city has seven railway stations
travel.road: Well connected via NH-58 and the Delhi-Meerut Expressway; city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis available
